H1: political alignment (categorical, IV) will impact gender equality attitudes (continuous, DV)

H2: Daily social media use will be positively correlated with the evaluation of importance of attractiveness in a relationship

## 1. Load the package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
#load the codebook package
library(codebook)
library(dplyr)

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw <-read.csv("data_doctored.csv")

#check row and column counts, and inspect the first few rows
dim(raw)
head(raw)

#make data with ID, sex at birth, relationship status, Attract_importance_1, qoa, and prqc_4-6; keep raw unchanged
data <- raw[,c("ResponseId", "Time_social_media_1",
               "Attract_importance_1", "cot_politics",
               "Gender_Equality_1","Gender_Equality_2", "Gender_Equality_3")]






```


## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r participant_ids}

#count na
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))
#count blank
sum(data$ResponseId=="",na.rm=TRUE)
#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))
#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
data[missingID,]
#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

```


## 3. Recode political views

```{r cot_politics}
# codebook: 1=far left, 2=center left, 3=center, 4=center right, 5=far right
table(data$cot_politics,useNA="ifany")

#turn cot_politics into a factor with labels FarLeft, CenterLeft, Center, CenterRight, FarRight
data$cot_politics <- factor(data$cot_politics,
                            levels= c(1,2,3,4,5),
                            labels= c("Far Left","Center Left","Center","Center Right","Far Right"))

table(data$cot_politics,useNA="ifany")

```


## 4. Validate views on gender

```{r genderviewvars}
#ensure Gender view data is numerical

data$Gender_Equality_1 <- as.numeric(data[,"Gender_Equality_1"], na.rm = FALSE)
data$Gender_Equality_2 <- as.numeric(data[,"Gender_Equality_2"], na.rm = FALSE)
data$Gender_Equality_3 <- as.numeric(data[,"Gender_Equality_3"], na.rm = FALSE)

#group all six Gender_equality_ variables
genderviewvars <- c("Gender_Equality_1","Gender_Equality_2", "Gender_Equality_3")

#reverse score the gender views so that higher score corresponds to less traditional
data[, genderviewvars] <- 8 - data[, genderviewvars]

#see summary of variables
summary(data[,genderviewvars])

#count NAs
colSums(is.na(data[,genderviewvars]))

#calculate total score; leave the total NA if any item is missing
data$viewtotal<- rowSums(data[,genderviewvars], na.rm=FALSE)


#review summary of variables with newly reversed scores
summary(data$viewtotal)

#count those that do not fall within expected sum range (3-21)
#SPECIFY IN CODEBOOK THIS IS SUM
sum(data$viewtotal >21 | data$viewtotal<3, na.rm= TRUE)

#check that each observed allocation is between 1 and 7
data$viewrange <- rowSums(
  data[,genderviewvars] < 1 | data[,genderviewvars] > 7,
  na.rm=TRUE
) ==FALSE


#define viewValid: total present, and each item in range
data$viewValid <- !is.na(data$viewtotal)

table(data$viewValid)

#remove FALSE rows
h1data <- filter(data, data$viewValid == TRUE & data$viewrange == TRUE)


#make h1Data with ID, cot_politics, and genderview
h1data <- h1data[c("ResponseId","cot_politics", "viewtotal")]

#remove NA in politics column
h1data <- na.omit(h1data)
```


## 5. Validating Social Media Use for H2
```{r media use}
#count those with minutes not  between expected range
sum(data$Time_social_media_1 >360 | data$Time_social_media_1<0, na.rm= TRUE)

#everyone is within the correct range!

#remove NA reports
data$mediaValid <- !is.na(data$Time_social_media_1)
h2data <- na.omit(data)

```

## 6. Validate Importance of Attractiveness Data

```{r attractiveness data}

#see summary of the importance of attractiveness 
summary(data$Attract_importance_1)

#count NAs
sum(is.na(data$Attract_importance_1))

#count those that do not fall within expected sum range (1-9)
sum(data$Attract_importance_1 >9 | data$Attract_importance_1<1, na.rm= TRUE)

#define attractValid: total present, and each item in range
data$attractvalid <- !is.na(data$Attract_importance_1)

table(data$attractvalid)

#remove FALSE rows
h2data <- filter(data, data$attractvalid == TRUE)

#make h2 data with relevant columns
h2data <- h2data[c("ResponseId","Time_social_media_1", "Attract_importance_1")]





```
##7. Make h2 data fram
```{r}

#make h1Data with ID, cot_politics, and genderview
h2data <- h2data[c("ResponseId","Time_social_media_1", "Attract_importance_1")]

#remove NA in politics column
h2data <- na.omit(h2data)

```


## 8. Check the final tables

```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(h1data)
str(h1data)
head(h1data)
colSums(is.na(h1data))
table(h1data$cot_politics,useNA="ifany")
range(h1data$viewtotal)
sum(duplicated(h1data$ResponseId))

#do the same for h2 data
dim(h2data)
str(h2data)
head(h2data)
colSums(is.na(h2data))
range(h2data$Time_social_media_1)
sum(duplicated(h2data$ResponseId))
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks (DO THIS TOO!!!!!!)

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r variable_labels} 
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(h1data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Political Alignment: original codes 1=Far Left, 2= Center Left, 3=Center, 4=Center Right, 5=Far Right; now stored as a factor",
  "Composite score of views on gender equality, lower score corresponds to more traditional gender roles"
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h2data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Average daily time spent using social media measured in minutes",
  "Importance placed on looking attractive, composite score"
)

```

H1 includes participants with an ID, a valid sex-at-birth category, and six
allocations between 0 and 30 that total 30. Factor level numbers in the
generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1data)

```

H2 includes participants with an ID, relationship status 1, 2, or 3, and
valid nonmissing qoa and at least one valid commitment response.

```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2data)

```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1data,"data/processed_data/221A_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2data,"data/processed_data/221A_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/221A_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/221A_h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
